analysis.title: September credit delinquencies improve as originations continue to grow
key_insights: September 2026 non-mortgage consumer credit delinquencies improved y/y: 60+ day bankcard 2.74% vs 2.83% a year ago, personal loan 3.26% vs 3.28%, auto 1.50% vs 1.57%. Card and auto remain above their long-term averages since 2009 (2.50% and 1.02%), personal loan is below its 3.76% average.
Lower-tier performance is mixed. Subprime and near-prime delinquencies rose in cards and personal loans, while subprime auto improved (9.18% vs 9.42%) and near-prime auto was unchanged at 0.60%.

Credit supply is growing. July originations rose 2.7% y/y in cards, 10.9% in personal loans and 1.3% in auto. GS says continued delinquency improvement could support a gradual easing of underwriting standards.

Mortgage 90+ day delinquency rose to 1.01% from 0.73% a year ago but is well below the 2.47% long-term average. GS sees limited risk of a broad wave of defaults, while high rates, low inventory and high home prices constrain affordability and purchase activity.
Mortgage originations rose 21.1% y/y in July, slowing from 28.0% in June. The 30-year mortgage rate was 7.2% as of October 29. Home prices rose 0.5% y/y in September.

Broader consumer indicators are mixed. Unemployment rose to 4.2% in September from 4.1% in August (long-term average 5.6%), real wages fell 0.7% y/y, and the savings rate was 4.1% in August vs a 5.8% average. Household debt is 57.8% of GDP (average 69.5%) and debt service is 11.1% of disposable income (average 12.4%).

Card originations: prime up 0.4% and subprime up 11.3% in July. Card balances are $1.2tn, up 3.3% y/y. Subprime 90+ day card delinquency was stable at 20.71% vs 20.70%, near-prime rose to 1.48% from 1.40%.

Personal loan originations have grown y/y for 18 consecutive months, 13 of them at double digits. Subprime originations rose 17.0% and prime 7.4% in July. Subprime 60+ day personal loan delinquency rose to 14.77% from 13.59% and near-prime to 1.21% from 1.09%.
Auto originations rose 1.3% y/y in July after a 0.9% decline in June (prime down 0.3%, subprime up 9.4%). The tariff-related pull-forward earlier in 2025 creates a tougher comparison.

GS favors Buy-rated FICO for pricing power, its position in credit decisioning and EPS growth. Risks are the FHFA unified mortgage pricing grid, broader VantageScore availability and a possible shift to bi-merge, which raise uncertainty on mortgage pricing, volumes and share.

FICO mortgage origination revenue grew 97% y/y in F3Q after 127% in F2Q and is now 62% of Scores revenue. Platform ARR growth accelerated to 62% y/y from 49%, and Platform ARR exceeded non-Platform ARR for the first time.

FICO's Mortgage Direct License Program, approved by the FHFA Director, has signed agreements covering about 73% of reseller volume, with potential coverage near 90% if another large reseller signs. It adds pricing flexibility and could offset VantageScore, waterfalling and bi-merge pressure.

EFX (Neutral): EWS Verifier diversified revenue grew 13% y/y in 3Q. EFX expects substantially all of $150mn of new state ACV signed year-to-date to contribute in 2027. VantageScore is used by about 2,000 lenders, with volumes up more than 230% since April. Offsetting this, current run rates imply a high-single-digit decline in 2027 mortgage market transactions and bi-merge carries about $80mn of annual revenue exposure before mitigation.

TRU (Neutral): revenue excluding mortgage grew about 5.5% y/y and auto grew 13%. Mortgage inquiries fell 16% y/y in 3Q and TRU expects a decline of more than 20% in 4Q, slowing OCC revenue growth ex-FICO royalties to 3-5% from about 5.5%. A full shift to bi-merge would cost about $33mn of annual revenue and $0.15 of EPS before mitigation. Higher interest expense is a roughly $60mn headwind in 2027.

market_movers.rationale: Pricing power, entrenched position in credit decisioning, mortgage direct license program and Software transformation support double-digit EPS growth. Regulatory and competitive uncertainty justifies a lower multiple. The PT was cut from $1,129 on 10/2/26.
EWS, government and VantageScore momentum are balanced by mortgage weakness, bi-merge exposure and slowing FI, auto and hiring activity. The PT was raised from $148 on 10/2/26.

Resilient non-mortgage growth, Insurance momentum and OneTru savings are offset by falling mortgage inquiries, lower margin expansion and higher interest expense. The PT was raised from $68 on 10/2/26.

sector_views.rationale: GS favors business models with pricing power, leading market positions, recurring revenue and durable earnings growth amid uneven consumer credit and mortgage ecosystem uncertainty. FICO is preferred over EFX and TRU.

earnings_insights: FICO F3Q (reported, per GS): mortgage origination revenue +97% y/y after +127% in F2Q. Platform ARR +62% y/y vs +49% prior quarter. GS Sept-26E adjusted EPS $11.11 and FY2026E adjusted EPS $43.01 (GS estimates). Valuation uses 18.0x NTM+1 EPS of $53.39.

EFX 3Q (reported, per GS): EWS Verifier diversified revenue +13% y/y. Company outlook is 100 bps of ex-FICO EBITDA margin expansion, with an $80mn mortgage revenue shortfall vs its prior outlook. GS FY2026E adjusted EPS $8.53 and FY2027E $10.06 (GS estimates). Valuation uses 14.25x NTM+1 EPS of $11.83.

TRU 3Q (reported, per GS): revenue excluding mortgage +~5.5% y/y, auto +13%. 4Q outlook (company guidance): mortgage inquiries down more than 20% y/y, OCC revenue growth ex-FICO royalties 3-5%. 2026 underlying margin expansion outlook cut to flat to 20 bps. GS FY2026E adjusted EPS $4.87 and FY2027E $5.55 (GS estimates). Valuation uses 12.5x NTM+1 EPS of $6.26.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Up from 4.1% in August but below the 5.6% average since 1990.
Modest pressure on consumer purchasing power.
Below the 5.8% average since 1998, a thinner consumer buffer.
Still elevated, constraining housing affordability and mortgage volumes.
Housing is holding up despite high mortgage rates.
Below the 69.5% average since 2003, so leverage compares favorably with history.

macro_indicators.indicator: Debt service as share of disposable income

trade_ideas.description: Buy-rated Fair Isaac (FICO) as GS's preferred name in business and information services, 12-month PT $961
trade_ideas.rationale: Pricing power, entrenched position in credit decisioning, robust EPS growth, Mortgage Direct License Program and Software transformation.
trade_ideas.risk: Inability to sustain elevated Scores price increases, competitive threats, macro and credit downturn, weak traction in decision management software, and FHFA pricing grid or bi-merge pressure on mortgage volumes.

risk_factors: Unified FHFA mortgage pricing grid and a possible shift to bi-merge could reduce mortgage score volumes, pricing and market share (FICO, EFX, TRU).
Broader VantageScore availability and adoption (about 35% of mortgage credit pulls at TRU) pressures Classic FICO share.
Mortgage volume weakness: EFX run rates imply a high-single-digit decline in 2027 mortgage transactions, and TRU mortgage inquiries fell 16% in 3Q with a fall of more than 20% expected in 4Q.
Subprime and near-prime delinquencies are rising in cards and personal loans.
Real wages are falling, the savings rate is low and unemployment is edging up.
EFX margin and revenue pressure from the $80mn mortgage revenue shortfall and about $80mn of bi-merge exposure.
TRU higher interest expense (about $60mn headwind in 2027) and reinvestment and legal costs.
Macro and credit downturn, interest rate risk and subprime origination headwinds.

tension_points.bull_case: FICO's Mortgage Direct License Program (agreements covering about 73% of reseller volume) gives it a new distribution channel and pricing flexibility, and mortgage origination revenue grew 97% y/y in F3Q.
tension_points.bear_case: The FHFA's unified mortgage pricing grid, broader VantageScore availability and a possible bi-merge transition could cut mortgage score volumes, pricing and share. EFX has about $80mn and TRU about $33mn of annual revenue exposure to bi-merge before mitigation.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A complete shift of FHFA-regulated loans to bi-merge, or failure of another large reseller to sign the Direct License Program, would weaken the FICO thesis.

tension_points.bull_case: Bankcard, personal loan and auto delinquencies improved y/y in September and originations are growing in all three categories, which could support easier underwriting.
tension_points.bear_case: Card and auto delinquencies remain above long-term averages, subprime and near-prime delinquencies rose in cards and personal loans, real wages fell 0.7% y/y and the savings rate is 4.1%.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Unemployment moving higher from 4.2% or delinquency improvement reversing would undercut the constructive credit view.
